holidays.name: National Kazoo Day
holidays.description: A day for buzzing, humming and honking along on the world's silliest instrument. No musical talent is required, and the kazoo works in any key you can hum. Grab one and start an office parade, a living-room marching band or a very questionable solo.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, and its founder is unclear. The kazoo itself grew out of 19th-century American novelty instruments. It is closely tied to Georgia, where early kazoos were made.
holidays.funFact: A kazoo doesn't work by blowing air through it. You hum or sing into it, and a thin membrane inside vibrates to add that buzzy sound.

holidays.name: International Lego Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the colorful plastic bricks that have launched countless castles, spaceships and painful midnight barefoot steps. Builders of all ages dig out their bins and make something new, whether it's a tiny car or an enormous tower.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the Lego brick patent, filed in Denmark on January 28, 1958. That design gave the bricks their famous interlocking stud-and-tube system.
holidays.funFact: Lego bricks made decades ago still click together with bricks made today. That is part of why the company is so well known for compatibility.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Pancake Day
holidays.description: A day to stack up fluffy pancakes studded with juicy blueberries and drown them in syrup. It is breakfast-for-any-meal permission, whether you use fresh berries, frozen ones or a boxed mix.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated each year as a delicious way to brighten the middle of winter.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America. Wild blueberries were gathered and eaten by Indigenous peoples long before pancakes topped with them became a breakfast staple.
